[center][size=4][b]Build Stardew Valley events visually, directly inside the game.[/b][/size][/center]
[center][size=4]Place actors on the map, build the scene on a timeline, preview it, then export the finished event into your own Stardew Valley project.[/size][/center]

[center][size=4]Event Studio is a visual editor for Stardew Valley's existing Event system. Exported scenes remain normal Stardew Valley event data and don't depend on a custom cutscene runtime.[/size][/center]

[heading][size=5]Actors[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The actor browser searches by display name and internal ID. Starting actors are placed directly on map tiles.[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Click an actor to select it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Use [b]Shift + Click[/b] for multi-selection.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Drag a starting actor to change its initial tile.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Moving several selected actors keeps their relative formation.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Press [b]F[/b] to rotate the selected actor.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Initial position, facing and editor color are available through the Inspector.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Temporary actors appear once their creation Action has been reached on the Timeline. The [b]farmer[/b] actor represents the player inside the event.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Timeline[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The Timeline controls the order of the event. It has two views of the same sequence.[/size]

[size=4][b]Tracks[/b] shows separate actor, dialogue, camera and other tracks. The vertical playhead marks the current preview position.[/size]

[size=4][b]Sequence[/b] shows the event as numbered cards in execution order. Cards can be dragged to reorder the scene.[/size]

[size=4]Switching views doesn't create a second timeline or change the event structure.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Environment[/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]Scene > Environment[/b] changes the editor's temporary season, weather and time of day.[/size]

[size=4]These values are used for the Studio and preview. Event-entry requirements are configured separately in [b]Export > Conditions[/b]. Setting the Canvas to winter, for example, doesn't make the event winter-only.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Preview[/size][/heading]
[table][tr][th][size=4]Preview[/size][/th]
[th][size=4]Best for[/size][/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4][b]Canvas Preview[/b][/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Fast iteration, Timeline editing and scene inspection[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4][b]In-game Preview[/b][/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Testing through Stardew Valley's Event runtime[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[size=4][b]Canvas Preview[/b] runs inside Event Studio and lets you play, pause and seek through the scene without leaving the workspace.[/size]

[size=4][b]In-game Preview[/b] creates a Stardew Valley Event and runs supported commands through the game's own Event runtime.[/size]

[size=4]Commands that can change the save or world in ways Event Studio can't restore safely may be blocked or simulated during preview. Test the exported event normally before release.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Import existing events[/size][/heading]
[size=4][b]Loaded Events[/b][/size]
[size=4]Scene > Loaded Events reads the current location's final loaded [i]Data/Events[/i] asset, including Content Patcher changes that have already been applied. Importing creates a new Event Studio project and leaves the source mod untouched.[/size]

[size=4][b]Raw Event[/b][/size]
[size=4]Paste a normal Stardew Valley event script to import it directly. Recognized commands become structured Actions. Unknown commands stay as [b]Raw[/b] so the original text isn't lost.[/size]

[size=4]Event Studio stores editable scenes as [i].svesproject[/i] files.[/size]

[/list][size=4]Timed autosave is enabled by default with a 45 second interval and can be changed in Settings.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Export[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Export is the handoff from Event Studio to your normal Stardew Valley mod project. Once the scene is finished, you can generate the event data and keep working with it outside the editor.[/size]

[size=4][b]Complete Mod[/b][/size]
[size=4]Creates a standalone Content Patcher pack for the current project and its related Fork branches. It's useful for testing, small standalone releases and checking the generated structure.[/size]

[size=4][b]Event Files[/b][/size]
[size=4]Exports the event and localization files without creating a separate complete mod. Use this when the scene belongs to a larger Content Patcher project.[/size]

[size=4][b]Copy[/b][/size]
[size=4]The event script, Forks, translations and complete event patches can also be copied directly to the clipboard.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Multiple cutscenes in one mod[/size][/heading]
[size=4]A Content Patcher mod can contain as many separate events as you need. Event Studio currently keeps independent scenes in separate [i].svesproject[/i] files and doesn't merge several projects into one Complete Mod export automatically.[/size]

[size=4]For a larger mod:[/size]
[list=1]
[*][size=4]Create each independent cutscene as its own Event Studio project.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Export each one with [b]Event Files[/b].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Move the generated event files into your existing Content Patcher project.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Add the corresponding Includes to your [i]content.json[/i].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Merge the generated localization entries where needed.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Complete Mod is there for convenience. Event Files is the better fit when Event Studio is one part of a larger modding workflow.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Actions and documentation[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Most Actions in Event Studio are visual editors for commands already provided by Stardew Valley. The [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Event_data]Official Stardew Valley Wiki - Modding: Event data[/url] already documents their syntax, arguments and vanilla behavior.[/size]

[size=4]Event Studio documentation is mainly about the editor itself: where a tool is, how its visual controls work, Timeline behavior, Preview, projects, importing and exporting.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Interface language and font support[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Event Studio uses [b]SMAPI i18n[/b] for interface text. The main release currently includes English, and other languages can be added through normal i18n files.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Community translations[/size][/heading]
[size=4]Anyone can create and publish a separate translation page for Event Studio.[/size]

[size=4]Translation releases may contain the translated or adapted [b]i18n files only[/b]. Don't bundle Event Studio DLLs, assets or other original mod files with the translation.[/size]

[size=4]Users still need to download and install the original Event Studio from its official page, then install the translation alongside it.[/size]

[tr][td][size=4]Original Event Studio assets[/size][/td]
[td][size=4][b]No[/b][/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]Other original Event Studio files[/size][/td]
[td][size=4][b]No[/b][/size][/td]
[/tr]

[/tr]
[/table]
[size=4]This also keeps translation pages independent from Event Studio releases, so users get the current original files from the main mod page.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Supported interface glyphs[/size][/heading]
[size=4]The interface uses bundled [b]Noto Sans[/b] texture atlases instead of system fonts.[/size]

[table][tr][th][size=4]Unicode range[/size][/th]
[th][size=4]Coverage[/size][/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]U+0020-U+007E[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Basic Latin[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]U+00A0-U+024F[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Latin-1 + Latin Extended-A/B[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]U+0400-U+052F[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]Cyrillic + Cyrillic Supplement[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][size=4]U+2000-U+206F[/size][/td]
[td][size=4]General punctuation[/size][/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[size=4]That covers most languages written with Latin or Cyrillic characters, including English, Polish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Czech, Slovak, Romanian, Hungarian, Turkish, Swedish, Finnish, Lithuanian, Latvian, Croatian, Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Bulgarian and Serbian Cyrillic.[/size]

[size=4]Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew and Thai scripts aren't included in the current UI atlas. Unsupported interface glyphs appear as [b]?[/b].[/size]

[size=4]This only affects text rendering inside Event Studio. Exported events still use normal Stardew Valley and Content Patcher text data.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Installation[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4]Install [url=https://smapi.io][b]SMAPI 4.5.0 or newer[/b][/url].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Extract Event Studio into [i]Stardew Valley/Mods[/i].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Load a single-player save.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Press [b]F10[/b].[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]You can also open the editor from the SMAPI console with:  [b]eventstudio[/b][/size]

[size=4]Event Studio itself runs without Content Patcher. You only need Content Patcher to install and run a Content Patcher pack created through Export.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Basic workflow[/size][/heading]
[center][size=4][b]Load location > F10 > New > place actors > add Actions > arrange Timeline > Preview > configure conditions > Export[/b][/size][/center]

[size=4]The scene can be designed almost entirely inside Event Studio. After export, the result can be handled like normal Stardew Valley event data.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Limitations[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*][size=4]Single-player only.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Some vanilla and mod-provided commands don't have a dedicated visual editor.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unsupported commands may remain Raw.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Independent projects aren't automatically merged into one Complete Mod.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Canvas Preview approximates some parts of the final event.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Some mod-specific rendering and runtime behavior can't be reproduced exactly.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]In-game Preview avoids operations that can't be restored safely.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Modded characters, maps, textures and custom commands still require the mods that provide them.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]The bundled UI font currently focuses on Latin and Cyrillic scripts.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]The exported scene still runs through Stardew Valley's Event system, so normal in-game testing is the final check before release.[/size]

[heading][size=5]Feedback and bug reports[/size][/heading]
[size=4]For reproducible bugs, include as much of this as possible:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4]Event Studio version.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Stardew Valley and SMAPI versions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]SMAPI log.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Reproduction steps.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]The affected .svesproject when possible.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Screenshots for UI problems.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]The mod providing the affected character, map, sprite or other resource when relevant.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Workflow feedback is useful too, especially when something takes too many steps, feels unclear, behaves differently in Preview, or still has to be handled manually.[/size]
